subject: loading a variable onto a factor negatively

messages.author: 68be3738a39ec32b
messages.subject: loading a variable onto a factor negatively
parts:
I have almost everything figured out in lavaan and think it’s an amazing package. I have one remaining question that I can’t figure out.

In EQS, you define observed variables in terms of their loading onto a factor.  In the example below, variable 1 (V1) loads positively onto factor 1 (F1), but negatively onto factor 2 (F2) as evidenced by the "-" before F2.  

14  /EQUATIONS                                                                     

    15  V1 =   *F1 - *F2 + E1;                                                         

    16  V2 =   *F1 - *F3 + E2;                                                         

etc...


Because the only way to load a variable onto a factor in lavaan is by adding it , like this:  

f1=~comp1.12+comp1.13+comp2.12+comp2.13
etc.

I don’t have any way of saying that one of those variables should actually load onto the factor negatively.

How would you suggest I do that?

Thanks ahead of time.

Mark

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: loading a variable onto a factor negatively
parts:
You could reverse-code the indicators so that it is positively correlated with the common factor -- that is generally recommended anyway.  But if you have a reason to leave it negatively correlated with the common factor, you can provide start values that push the optimizer in the right direction to find the optimal solution.  For example, if the third indicator is the one you expect to be negatively correlated with the common factor:

f1 =~ start(1.0)*comp1.12 + start(1.0)*comp1.13 + start(-1.0)*comp2.12 + start(1.0)*comp2.13

The above example assumes you are standardizing the latent variable (std.lv = TRUE) and estimating all factor loadings, but that is not necessary.

Terry

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: loading a variable onto a factor negatively
parts:
Mark,
I am not sure how EQS interprets the minus sign.  If you want to constrain the loading to be negative rather than just nudge Lavaan in that direction, you could use a method described by David Rindskopf (1984).  G1 and G2 are phantom variables.  The "loading" parameter is your constrained factor loading.  As a caution, I was not able to get this to converge without providing positive start values for the "a" parameter although the start values did not have to be close to the correct values.

# Begin code
require(lavaan)
sessionInfo()


simMod <- '
F =~ 1*i1 + 1*i2 + 1*i3 + 1*i4 + -1*i5
F ~~ 1 * F
i1 ~~ .5 * i1
i2 ~~ .5 * i2
i3 ~~ .5 * i3
i4 ~~ .5 * i4
i5 ~~ .5 * i5
'

simData <- simulateData(simMod)
round(cov(simData),2)

fitMod <- '
F =~ i1 + i2 + i3 + i4
G1 =~ 0
G2 =~ 0
i5 ~ -1*G2
G2 ~ label("a")*G1 + start(.5)*G1
G1 ~ label("a")*F + start(.5)*F
F~~1*F
G1~~0*G1
G2~~0*G2
i1~~i1
i2~~i2
i3~~i3
i4~~i4
i5~~ i5
loading := a*a*-1
'

lavParTable(fitMod)

fit <- lavaan(fitMod, simData)
summary(fit)
# End code

Keith

Rindskopf, D. (1984). Using phantom and imaginary latent variables to parameterize constraints in linear structural models.Psychometrika, 49, 37-47.

----------------
Keith A. Markus
John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY
